items.question: Is var dynamically typed?
items.answer: No. The compiler infers a single static type from the initializer. IL is the same as writing the type. It is unrelated to JavaScript var and to dynamic.
followUps: What if the initializer is null?
items.sixtySeconds: var is inference. Still static. Needs an initializer. Not JS var, not dynamic.

items.question: Why decimal for grades and money?
items.answer: decimal is base-10. double is binary floating point like JS number — 0.1 + 0.2 style error. Use double for Skia transforms; decimal for GPA and fees.
followUps: What is the default of bool?
items.sixtySeconds: decimal for money/grades. double for measurements. string is a reference type.

items.question: Value type versus reference type?
items.answer: Assignment copies the value or copies the reference. Boxing wraps a value as object. Do not claim structs always live on the stack; GC details are module 14.
followUps: What happens when you mutate a struct from a list indexer?
Why is string a reference type with == by content?
items.sixtySeconds: Copy data vs alias object. Boxing to object. Stack/heap is CLR, not the definition.

items.question: How is int? different from a null string?
items.answer: int? is Nullable<int>, a struct with HasValue. A null string is a reference with no object. Nullable reference annotations are module 07.
items.sixtySeconds: int? is a wrapper struct. string null is a missing reference. Locals must be assigned.

items.question: typeof vs GetType vs is vs dynamic vs TS any?
items.answer: typeof(T) is the compile-time Type. GetType() is the instance’s run-time type. is/as test compatibility. object is the CTS root. dynamic binds members at run time. TS any erases; unknown must be narrowed; C# has object and dynamic, not any/unknown.
followUps: Why is GetType() == typeof(Base) a bug?
When is boxing involved with object?
items.sixtySeconds: typeof compile-time, GetType run-time, is for compatibility. dynamic late-binds. Not TS any.
